title: Morning Has Already Started
summary: Carrie arrives with a plan and discovers that the household has already divided the morning into ordinary individual errands without waiting for her.
panelPlan: Wide: 5B is already in motion. First Male Kin ties off the laundry bag; Second Male Kin finishes breakfast and checks his transit card; Astrid puts a small reusable bag over one shoulder; Gunnar closes a library book; Bjorn drinks coffee.
Medium: Carrie enters with a folder, already speaking.
Close on Carrie: She stops when nobody turns toward her for assignments.
Medium: Bjorn lifts his coffee slightly, acknowledging her without interrupting the household motion.
Wide: Everyone continues preparing to leave.

dialogueInline.text: Since when do you all have separate mornings?

source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: Downstairs
summary: At the building entrance the household splits naturally toward separate routines, and Carrie realizes nobody is waiting for a group itinerary.
settingText: Bushwick apartment hallway, stoop and sidewalk
panelPlan: Wide: The group descends together through the fifth-floor hallway and stairs.

Exterior wide: At the stoop, First Male Kin turns toward the laundromat with the bag; Second Male Kin heads toward the subway direction; Astrid crosses toward the neighborhood side street; Gunnar heads toward the library route.
Medium on Carrie: She half-turns from one departing person to another.
Two-shot: Bjorn remains beside her, untroubled.
Wide: The four routes separate into ordinary foot traffic.

dialogueInline.text: Yes, Gunnar. I got the concept.
That's not the same as knowing where you're going.

source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: No Itinerary
summary: Carrie's instinct to account for everyone collides with Bjorn's newer acceptance that adults can leave home without reporting a route.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie looks down the three directions the Kin just took.
Two-shot: She asks Bjorn which destination belongs to which person.
Close on Bjorn: He genuinely does not know all of them.
Close on Carrie: She waits for concern that does not come.
Wide: Gunnar continues toward the corner, then stops when he realizes Carrie and Bjorn have not moved.
source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: Your List
summary: Carrie's planned casework increasingly describes tasks the household has already completed or knows how to complete itself.
panelPlan: Medium walking three-shot: Carrie finally opens the folder while they head down the block.
Insert: Her handwritten task list is shown only as a few recipe-required items: laundry, groceries, library return, transit refill.
Medium: Gunnar identifies which tasks are already underway.
Close on Carrie: She crosses out several lines.
Wide: The three continue walking, the folder visibly thinner in purpose than when she arrived.
source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: A Route Carrie Did Not Teach
summary: Gunnar chooses a route based on his own familiarity with the neighborhood, and Carrie follows rather than directing.
panelPlan: Wide: Gunnar turns onto a side street before Carrie indicates any direction.
Medium: Carrie notices and checks the cross street.
Two-shot: Gunnar explains that this route avoids a recurring delivery blockage and reaches the library from the quieter side.
Medium on Bjorn: He follows Gunnar without comment.
Wide: Carrie tucks the folder under her arm and simply follows.

dialogueInline.text: Truck blocks the corner after nine.

source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: Still Useful
summary: Carrie briefly mistakes decreasing dependence for decreasing usefulness; Bjorn corrects the premise without returning her to managerial control.
settingText: Bushwick neighborhood sidewalk outside library route
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie closes the folder after another item becomes unnecessary.
Two-shot: She makes a dry comment about becoming obsolete.
Close on Bjorn: He rejects the idea immediately but does not hand her control back.
Medium: Gunnar gestures toward the remaining city paperwork in her folder.
Wide: Carrie looks at the two of them, then at the folder, accepting the distinction.

dialogueInline.text: We still don't know what half your papers mean.

source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: Garbage Night
summary: That evening, the Vikings encounter New York's curbside discard system and see usable material where the city sees removal.
settingText: Bushwick apartment block at dusk, garbage night
panelPlan: Wide: Evening curb outside the apartment building. Ordinary trash bags and a few discarded household objects have been placed out for collection; among them is a broken solid-wood shelving unit or cabinet side with usable clean boards.
Medium: First Male Kin stops at the usable wood. Bjorn and Gunnar examine it without touching closed bags or personal items.
Close: Bjorn tests one exposed board for rot and finds most of it sound.
Medium: Carrie exits the building and finds them evaluating the pile.
Wide: Foot traffic continues around the curb.
source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

directionInline.text: Show clearly discarded curbside material, not theft from an occupied stoop or private property. The useful wood should be plausible salvage, not pristine furniture.

title: If It Is Out
summary: Carrie gives the only distinction that matters: discarded material may be reused, but they must not treat every unattended object as available.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie points to the organized curbside discard pile, then separately to a bicycle locked to a railing and a planter near a stoop.
Two-shot: Gunnar states the rule back in practical terms.
Medium: First Male Kin lifts only the loose clean board from the discard pile.
Close on Carrie: She confirms he chose correctly.
Wide: They carry the board toward the building while leaving the rest of the curb undisturbed.

dialogueInline.text: If it's actually put out for trash, that's different.

source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: Keep the Sidewalk Clear
summary: A sanitation worker gives one practical instruction and the Vikings obey it immediately, reinforcing that city authority is often functional and local rather than ceremonial.
panelPlan: Wide: A sanitation truck arrives farther down the block; workers in reflective workwear move efficiently among curb piles.
Medium: Bjorn, Gunnar and First Male Kin have set the salvaged board briefly where it narrows pedestrian space while deciding how to carry it upstairs.
Medium: A sanitation worker gestures to the blocked path and gives one concise instruction.
Medium: The three move the board immediately against the building edge, opening the sidewalk.
Wide: The worker continues the route without further interaction; pedestrians pass through the cleared space.
source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: Who Is In Charge
summary: Gunnar notices that the sanitation worker's authority came entirely from responsibility for the immediate work, not from ceremony or armed status.
settingText: Bushwick sidewalk after sanitation truck passes
panelPlan: Medium: The three watch the sanitation truck continue down the block.
Close on Gunnar: He follows how pedestrians, drivers and curbside workers briefly reorganize around the crew.
Two-shot: Bjorn asks what Gunnar is watching.
Medium: Gunnar answers in concrete terms.
Wide: First Male Kin shoulders one end of the board, ready to carry it upstairs.
source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: Useful Wood
summary: The salvaged material becomes household work rather than scavenging spectacle.
settingText: Bushwick rear alley / fire-escape work area, evening
panelPlan: Wide: In a practical rear work area near the building, the salvaged board rests on a stable improvised work surface with hand tools nearby.
Medium: First Male Kin removes damaged hardware and splits off the rotten end while Bjorn checks the remaining grain.
Close: Gunnar holds a short clean section and tests its weight.
Medium: Bjorn marks several smaller useful pieces rather than preserving the board as a single object.
Wide: Work continues under ordinary building light.
source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: Carving
summary: Bjorn and First Male Kin turn one piece of discarded wood into a small functional household object with unmistakable craft rather than generic decoration.
settingText: Bushwick rear alley / fire-escape work area
panelPlan: Medium: Bjorn carves a compact wall hook or bracket from one clean piece while First Male Kin shapes another piece for a small shelf support.
Close: The carving is restrained but skilled, with period-informed interlace or animal-form detail integrated into a functional object.
Medium: Gunnar sweeps shavings into a container rather than leaving debris in the alley.
Close: Bjorn tests the strength of the finished hook by hand.
Wide: Several useful pieces now sit where a discarded board had been.

dialogueInline.text: Too much work for a hook.

source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: You Made That
summary: The upstairs neighbor encounters the finished piece and responds to the craftsmanship as an ordinary fact about someone who lives in the building.
panelPlan: Medium: Bjorn and First Male Kin carry the finished hook/bracket and a small shelf piece toward 5B.
Two-shot: The Upstairs Neighbor exits their apartment and notices the carved object.
Close: The neighbor turns the piece slightly to see the craftsmanship but does not treat it like a museum artifact.
Medium: Bjorn answers the obvious question.
Wide: The neighbor continues downstairs while the Vikings enter 5B.
source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: A Place for the Key
summary: The discarded city material becomes part of the household's established geography when the carved hook is installed for the brass apartment key.
panelPlan: Wide: The small carved hook is installed securely near the apartment door, replacing the improvised place where the brass key has been kept.
Insert: Bjorn hangs the brass key on it.
Medium: Carrie arrives, notices the new object and recognizes the salvaged wood.
Two-shot: First Male Kin explains the source with no defensiveness.
Wide: The key, carved hook, neighborhood groceries, library books and ordinary apartment objects now coexist as one household.

dialogueInline.text: Now it has a better one.

source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: Locked Out
summary: On another day Carrie reaches 5B with her folder and discovers the apartment empty; the old privacy lesson has become normal household reality.
panelPlan: Wide: Carrie reaches the fifth-floor hallway carrying a folder and coffee.
Medium: She knocks on 5B. No answer.
Close: She automatically reaches toward the door, then stops because she does not have a key.
Insert: The locked handle remains still.
Wide: Carrie leans against the opposite wall to wait rather than trying to solve the absence.
source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: Gunnar Comes Home
summary: Gunnar returns independently, unlocks the apartment with his own household key access, and becomes the person who lets Carrie in.
panelPlan: Wide: Gunnar comes up the stairs carrying a library tote and a small grocery item, sees Carrie waiting and is unsurprised.
Medium: He takes out the apartment key.
Insert: Gunnar unlocks 5B.
Two-shot: Carrie follows him inside rather than entering first.
Medium: Gunnar sets the tote down in its established place.

dialogueInline.text: You could have gone for coffee.
Thank you for the hostage negotiation advice.

source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: Do You Know Where They Are
summary: Carrie discovers that Gunnar also does not know everyone's location, and his mild concern coexists with confidence that the household can navigate itself home.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie opens her folder at the table while Gunnar puts away his library book.
Two-shot: She asks where the others went.
Close on Gunnar: He gives the actual answer rather than pretending certainty.
Close on Carrie: She is almost relieved that he admits some concern.
Wide: The apartment remains empty except for the two of them and the established household objects.

dialogueInline.text: They have keys. They'll probably be back.

source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: First Back
summary: First Male Kin returns from the laundromat with folded clothes and an established complaint that no longer requires explanation.
panelPlan: Medium: The door unlocks from outside; First Male Kin enters carrying folded laundry.
Close: Carrie looks from the laundry to him, then toward the hallway as if expecting an escort.
Medium: He places the laundry in its established household location.
Two-shot: Gunnar asks the familiar question.
Wide: First Male Kin begins putting clothes away without further discussion.
source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: Second Back
summary: Second Male Kin returns from a self-chosen city excursion, establishing that he can travel for no purpose beyond wanting to see somewhere.
panelPlan: Wide: The apartment door opens again; Second Male Kin enters alone with wind-reddened cheeks and an inexpensive folded transit or waterfront paper tucked into a pocket.
Medium: Gunnar looks up from the table.
Two-shot: Carrie asks the simplest version of where he went, without turning it into an intake.
Close: He answers with a place, not an explanation.
Wide: He hangs his coat and rejoins the room.
source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: You All Have Places
summary: Astrid returns through the hallway already embedded in a small neighbor routine, and Carrie finally names what she has been watching all day.
settingText: Fifth-floor hallway and apartment doorway at dusk
panelPlan: Wide from inside 5B: Astrid approaches down the hallway at the same time as the Upstairs Neighbor comes from the stairs.
Medium: The neighbor gives Astrid a casual greeting and hands back a small reusable container or packaged-item wrapper from an earlier exchange; no explanation is offered.
Two-shot: Astrid answers without stopping and uses her own key at 5B.
Medium inside: Carrie watches Astrid enter and put away the small item.
Close on Carrie and Astrid.
source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.

title: Some
summary: Bjorn returns to a household that has reconverged without anyone arranging it; Carrie opens the folder she brought hours earlier and realizes only part of her work still belongs to her.
panelPlan: Wide: Bjorn enters last with his familiar coffee cup and a small ordinary purchase. Everyone else is already home doing separate evening tasks.
Medium: He takes in the room, then notices Carrie's still-unopened folder on the table.
Two-shot: Carrie finally opens it.
Medium: She looks from the remaining list to the household around her.
Two-shot: Bjorn asks whether she still needs the list.
Final wide: Carrie closes the folder to half its thickness and remains seated with them while evening continues.
source: Issue 10 — Belonging. Recovered separate-mornings / return-routes material plus new garbage-night / useful-things connective material.
